what: The rustup install command a reader will copy wraps inside a flag: `curl --proto '=https' --` / `tlsv1.2 -sSf`, so it reads as a separate `--` and `tlsv1.2` (a beginner typing it by eye gets a broken command).
evidence: `.cmdbox pre { white-space: pre-wrap; overflow-wrap: anywhere }` (rs-ch1.css:49) lets the browser break after the hyphen of `--tlsv1.2`. Crop: /tmp/claude-0/-home-claude/7f030446-3270-51d4-abc1-d3638614f9af/scratchpad/review-visual-rs-1-5/t1/m-01.png (column 4, panel 13). fix: Before → After (why): `.cmdbox pre { white-space: pre-wrap; overflow-wrap: anywhere; }` → `.cmdbox pre { white-space: pre; overflow-x: auto; }` (a command meant to be copied must never wrap inside a token; a sideways scroll keeps it exact). what: Chapter 4's three illustration animations break the engine's motion budget and cohesion: a 900ms drop with a 1.4 overshoot curve, a 1.4s switch wobble, and a 700ms slide plus a 500ms delay, next to engine entrances of 200-280ms.
evidence: rs-ch4.css:29-35: `.drop-me { animation: ch4-drop 900ms cubic-bezier(.3,.1,.4,1.4) }` (from translateY(-60px)), `.flip-me { animation: ch4-flip 1.4s ease-in-out }`, `.slide-me { animation: ch4-slide 700ms ease-out }`, `.slide-me.late { animation-delay: 500ms }`. DESIGN_SYSTEM §5: entrances `--dur-ui`/`--ease-out`; the engine's own machine feed was cut from 500ms to 240ms for the same reason. Reduced motion and "Animations: off" do stop them (global rule in comic.css:332/337).
fix: Before → After (why): `ch4-drop 900ms cubic-bezier(.3,.1,.4,1.4)` from `translateY(-60px)` → `ch4-drop var(--dur-move) var(--ease-out)` from `translateY(-24px) scale(.95); opacity: 0` (explanatory but seen once per panel; the engine's feed is 240ms, no overshoot) · `ch4-flip 1.4s ease-in-out` → `transform var(--dur-ui) var(--ease-out)`, one swing (a switch flips, it doesn't wobble) · `ch4-slide 700ms ease-out` + `animation-delay: 500ms` → `var(--dur-ui) var(--ease-out)` + `animation-delay: 60ms` (stagger 30-80ms; 500ms makes the second frame feel late).

what: Chapter 5's out-of-bounds animation ends with a label that grows from almost nothing (`scale(0.2)`), runs 4.1s in total, and its fall uses `ease-in`; the finish flag skews three times.
evidence: rs-ch5.css:84-91: `.hop-me 2.4s steps(6,end)`, `.fall-off 0.9s ease-in 2.5s`, `.late-pop 0.4s ease-out 3.2s` with `@keyframes ch5-late { 0% { transform: scale(0.2); opacity: 0 } }`, `.flag-wave 1s ease-in-out 3 alternate`. Emil standard 5: never animate from near zero; start at 0.9-0.97 + opacity. (The stepped hop is good explanatory motion and the gravity ease-in is defensible; the comment at rs-ch5.css:83 is out of date: the engine keeps `.motion` under reduced motion and stops animations with a global rule instead.)
fix: Before → After (why): `ch5-late 0.4s ease-out 3.2s`, from `scale(0.2)` → `var(--dur-ui) var(--ease-out) 3.2s`, from `scale(0.95); opacity: 0` (nothing appears from nothing) · `hop-me 2.4s` → `steps(6,end) 1.8s` (0.3s per cup still reads as hops; the whole story then ends under 3s) · `flag-wave … 3 alternate` → `1 alternate` or delete (decorative loop on a teaching drawing; it competes with the cones the caption is about).

what: The box drawings re-run the engine's `pop-in` at 420ms with the weak built-in `ease-out`, and keep a `bob` idle loop on a plain SVG group that the engine never pauses off screen.
evidence: rs-ch2.css:51 `.motion .panel.played .bx-hot { animation: pop-in 420ms ease-out 1 }`; :52 `.motion .bx-brick .bob { animation: bob 2.4s ease-in-out infinite }`. Engine pop-in is `var(--dur-ui) var(--ease-out)` (DESIGN_SYSTEM motion table), and `.idle-off` only pauses `svg.char` (DESIGN_SYSTEM §5.6).
fix: Before → After (why): `animation: pop-in 420ms ease-out 1` → `animation: pop-in var(--dur-ui) var(--ease-out) 1 both` (match the engine entrance; under 300ms) · `.bx-brick .bob { animation: bob 2.4s … infinite }` → put `class="char"`-style pausing on it or limit to `animation-iteration-count: 3` (an infinite loop nobody pauses runs while off screen).

what: The X-ray's part list is a hand-rolled toggle group (`.xr-jump`) instead of the engine's toggle (`.path-btn` / `.anat-keys button`): no `aria-pressed`, no `:active` press, no `touch-action`, and buttons only about 30px tall on phones.

what: The hanging-indent breaker breaks after `{` even inside a string literal, so format placeholders split across lines on phones: `println!("{` / `n}...");`, `println!("Thanks! {` / `price}");`, a lone `{` on its own row in spot lines.
evidence: rust ch5 P10 walker line 4 (/tmp/claude-0/-home-claude/7f030446-3270-51d4-abc1-d3638614f9af/scratchpad/review-visual-rs-1-5/t5/m-01.png), ch3 spot-the-bug lines 6 and boss 2 line 5 (/tmp/claude-0/-home-claude/7f030446-3270-51d4-abc1-d3638614f9af/scratchpad/review-visual-rs-1-5/t3/m-07.png), ch3 boss 4 parsons line 3, ch5 boss 5 line 4 (/tmp/claude-0/-home-claude/7f030446-3270-51d4-abc1-d3638614f9af/scratchpad/review-visual-rs-1-5/t5/m-08.png). DESIGN_SYSTEM §6 lists `{` as a break point, which suits code blocks but not a `{name}` hole inside quotes.
fix: In the break-point pass, skip `{` when the next characters match `[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_.]*(:[^}]*)?}` (a format hole), and never leave a lone `{` or `}` on a continuation row (prefer breaking at the previous space).

what: In the long `i32 × f64` case the lens highlights clue 7 on a line the reader can't see: `.lens-term` is capped at 30em with its own vertical scroll, and the lens never scrolls the highlighted line into view.
evidence: Stepped in the browser: case 0 lens-term scrollHeight 860px vs clientHeight 450px at 1280 (745 vs 378 at 390); clues 1-6 are visible, clue 7's `.lens-ln.hit` lies outside the box. rs-ch3.css:58 `max-height: 30em; overflow-y: auto`; rs-ch3.js mountLens has no scroll call. ch1's lens has no cap and stays correct.
fix: In rs-ch3.js after marking the hit line: `hit.scrollIntoView({ block: 'nearest', inline: 'nearest' })` scoped to the terminal (or `term.scrollTop = hit.offsetTop - term.clientHeight / 3`), or drop the cap: Before → After (why): `.lens-term { max-height: 30em; overflow-y: auto }` → `.lens-term { overflow-y: visible }` (a nested vertical scroller on a phone page hides the thing the step is pointing at).
